original_question: Let f ∈ Cv (z) be a rational function of degree at least 2, and let Jf ⊂ P1Berk be the Julia set of f . Then Jf ∩ P1 (Cv ) is equal to the closure in P1 (Cv ) of the set of Type I repelling periodic points of f.
target_in_paper: Conjecture 17.1 in Section 17 (p-adic and Nonarchimedean Dynamics): the paper conjectures that for a rational function f ∈ C_v(z) of degree at least 2, the Type I part of the Berkovich Julia set equals the closure in P^1(C_v) of the Type I repelling periodic points. citeturn9view0turn13view0
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's official formulation: it has the correct map f ∈ C_v(z), the correct degree restriction deg(f) ≥ 2, the correct ambient Julia set J_f ⊂ P^1_Berk, and the correct conclusion that J_f ∩ P^1(C_v) should equal the closure in P^1(C_v) of the Type I repelling periodic points. In substance, it is essentially Conjecture 17.1 almost verbatim. citeturn9view0turn11view4
missing_details: The paper first fixes the ambient field: C_v is assumed to be algebraically closed and complete for a nonarchimedean absolute value |·|_v satisfying the ultrametric inequality. citeturn13view0
P^1_Berk should be identified as the Berkovich projective line over C_v, and P^1(C_v) is its dense subset of Type I points. citeturn13view0turn13view1

The map f ∈ C_v(z) acts on P^1(C_v) and extends continuously to an endomorphism of P^1_Berk; the conjecture concerns the Julia set of this Berkovich extension. citeturn13view1turn13view2turn9view0
To be fully stand-alone, "Type I repelling periodic point" should be unpacked as a periodic point a ∈ P^1(C_v) whose multiplier λ_f(a) satisfies |λ_f(a)|_v > 1. citeturn13view2turn13view3
The paper presents this as a conjecture, not as a theorem or established result. citeturn9view0

No extra existence assumption should be added: the paper explicitly notes that J_f ∩ P^1(C_v) can be empty (for example, under good reduction), and separately notes Bézivin's result that the conjecture is true if f has at least one Type I repelling periodic point. citeturn9view0turn9view1
refined_question: Let C_v be an algebraically closed field complete with respect to a nonarchimedean absolute value |·|_v, let P^1_Berk be the Berkovich projective line over C_v, and let f ∈ C_v(z) be a rational function of degree at least 2, viewed as its natural extension f: P^1_Berk → P^1_Berk. If J_f denotes the Berkovich Julia set of f, is it true that the Type I part J_f ∩ P^1(C_v) is exactly the closure in P^1(C_v) of the set of Type I repelling periodic points of f, i.e. periodic points a ∈ P^1(C_v) with |λ_f(a)|_v > 1? citeturn9view0turn13view0turn13view1turn13view2turn13view3
justification: The draft is targeting Conjecture 17.1 exactly, not a broader neighboring problem. The surrounding discussion in Section 17 supplies the hidden setup: the nonarchimedean field C_v, the Berkovich line P^1_Berk containing P^1(C_v) as the Type I points, the extension of f to P^1_Berk, the multiplier-based notion of repelling periodic Type I points, and the definition of the Berkovich Julia set as the complement of the Berkovich Fatou set. Immediately after the conjecture, the paper records the two key nearby facts that frame the problem: Hsia proved the inclusion of J_f ∩ P^1(C_v) in the closure of all Type I periodic points, and Bézivin proved Conjecture 17.1 whenever f has at least one Type I repelling periodic point. These remarks confirm that the refined question should remain exactly at the level of the conjecture and should not be broadened or strengthened. citeturn13view0turn13view1turn13view2turn13view3turn9view0turn9view1
